title: GPU major release readiness and tenant communications playbook
author: Rina Patel
body:
Overview
-------
This playbook defines the operational runbook, Terraform/IaC gating, CI/CD checks, tenant communications, and rollback procedures for any major GPU fleet release (examples: runtime v2.0, kernel upgrade, heterogenous pool addition, or large-scale capacity rebalancing). It is intended for infra oncall, release engineers, SREs, and platform product managers.

Scope
-----
- Applies to planned releases that: change serving runtime binaries, change kernel/driver versions, add or migrate GPU instance types, or update node-level networking that may impact inference traffic.
- Excludes: small config-only patches that do not touch node images or routing policies. Those follow the standard small-change playbook.

Goals and success criteria
--------------------------
- No more than 0.5% increase in 5xx error rate for hosted inference during the 4 hour rollout window.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p90/p99 per-token generation for short requests (<=64 tokens) must not regress by >15% compared to baseline.
- Customer-impacting incidents must be resolved within 60 minutes.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Release Lead: coordinates cut, rollback and postmortem (example: Senior Release Engineer).
- Infra Oncall: first responder for incidents affecting fleet health (pager duty: infra-sre-oncall).
- Runtime Team: owners of serving runtime and kernel changes.
- Network Team: owner for egress/VPC changes.
- Customer Success: sends tenant communications and QBR updates.
- Security: approves images and signs the release bundle.

Pre-release gating checklist (must be green)
-------------------------------------------
1) IaC and images
   - Terraform plan approved and attached to PR. Command example: 
     terraform -chdir=iac/gpu-pools plan -var=release_tag=2026-02-10-v2
   - Pinned AMI/container digest documented in the release notes.
   - Image vulnerability scan: CVE threshold = no critical unpatched CVEs.

2) CI/CD and tests
   - Nightly end-to-end smoke tests (small sample) pass twice in a row in staging. CI job name: gpu-release-e2e-smoke.
   - Canary workload harness (100 tps synthetic) passes with no errors for 60 minutes. Job: canary-stability/major-release.
   - Kernel/driver compatibility matrix exercised by kube e2e matrix.

3) Capacity and placement validation
   - Forecasted capacity check: capacity headroom >= 20% for Dedicated and Hosted clusters during release window.
   - Cross-zone placement tested with simulated AZ failure.

4) Observability and alerting
   - Dashboards created: "Release: GPU Runtime vX.Y - Health" and shared with pager schedule.
   - Key alerts enabled and validated: GPU node ready < 95% for 5m, kv-cache hit rate drop > 20% from baseline, sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 15m.

5) Tenant communications
   - Pre-release email and Slack announcement scheduled 72 hours before release.
   - Maintenance page updated and scheduled on status.redwood.ai.

Pre-release checklist table (example)
------------------------------------
| Item | Owner | Must be green? | Evidence |
|------|-------|----------------|----------|
| Terraform plan | Infra IaC | Yes | PR #1234 + plan output attached |
| Image scan | Release Lead | Yes | Clair/Grafeas report (digest: sha256:abc) |
| Canary test | Runtime Team | Yes | canary-stability job logs |
| Capacity forecast | SRE | Yes | capacity-report-2026-02-10.csv |

Release day run steps (ordered)
-------------------------------
1. Pre-window (T-3h)
   - Announce start of pre-check on #infra-releases and ping oncall.
   - Verify runbook is accessible and the release lead has escalation contacts.
   - Run quick health queries:
     - Datadog query: avg(last_15m):p95(redwood.inference.latency) by {region}
     - Prometheus: rate(inference_request_errors_total[5m])

2. Canary rollout (T=0)
   - Deploy to canary pool limited to 1-2 nodes (or 1% traffic). Use deployment tag: release-canary-<tag>.
   - Monitor standard canary checks for 30–60 minutes: error rate, latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate.
   - Acceptance criteria: no >2x spike in p95 latency and error rate below 0.2% for 30 minutes.

3. Progressive rollout (T+60m)
   - If canary green, perform staged expansion to 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% of target pools. Each step: wait 20 minutes and validate.
   - Commands: 
     - terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool.canary -var=release_tag=<tag>
     - kubectl -n redwood rollout status deployment/gpu-runtime-canary --timeout=10m

4. Tenant routing changes
   - For hosted customers, modify Smart Routing policy to pin low-tier traffic to older model variant if regressions detected. Example API call: 
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/policies -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"policy":"pin-to-stable","percent":40}'

5. Post-rollout verification (T+4h)
   - Run automation validation suite (integration & load) for 2 hours.
   - Confirm backend metrics within threshold and no regression in quality metrics (if applicable).

Rollback procedure (fast path)
-----------------------------
- Trigger: sustained 5xx > 0.5% for >15 minutes OR p95 latency regression > 25% for 30 minutes.
- Steps:
  1) Pause progressive rollout and stop further terraform applies.
  2) Execute rollback artifacts (signed stable image):
     - terraform apply -var=release_tag=stable-2026-01-10 -target=module.gpu_pool.target
  3) For Kubernetes-managed runtime, perform: 
     kubectl -n redwood set image deployment/gpu-runtime <container>=registry.redwood.ai/gpu-runtime:stable-2026-01-10
     kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/gpu-runtime --to-revision=<stable-revision>
  4) Re-route traffic to stable model variants and notify Customer Success to contact impacted tenants.
  5) Open a SevX incident, assign incident commander, and run the incident checklist.

Fast mitigation (while rollback in progress)
------------------------------------------
- Increase instance autoscaling thresholds to add spare capacity: patch the HPA minReplicas to +20%.
- Reduce batching window temporarily via feature flag: featureflags.redwood/batching-window -> 10ms
- Switch to lower-cost model variant for non-critical traffic via routing policy.

Monitoring playbook: key queries and dashboards
----------------------------------------------
- GPU node readiness: kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready"} (expect >= 98%)
- Per-region p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
- KV cache hit rate: sum(kv_cache_hits) / sum(kv_cache_lookups) by (cluster)
- Prometheus alert examples:
  - alert: GPUNodeReadyDrop
    expr: (count(kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status!="true"}) > 0)
    for: 5m
  - alert: InferenceErrorSpike
    expr: increase(inference_request_errors_total[15m]) / increase(inference_requests_total[15m]) > 0.005

CI/CD gating and IaC patterns
----------------------------
- All Terraform changes for this release must be under a single release PR and reference the release_tag. PR must include plan output and test plan.
- Use feature branches with short-lived state workspaces: terraform workspace select release-<tag>.
- Image promotion: build -> scan -> sign -> push to release registry. Only signed images (in cosign) are allowed in the release.
- Canary jobs are required and must be auto-approved by the release lead before progressing.

Tenant communications (templates and cadence)
-------------------------------------------
1) T-72h: Preliminary notice (email + status page)\   Subject: Upcoming maintenance: GPU runtime updates on 2026-02-10\   Body: Short description, expected window, impact (possible brief increased latency), contact link.
2) T-2h: Reminder and live-link to status page and Slack.\3) T+1h (if no issues): Success note and summary of changes with link to release notes.\4) If rollback happens: Immediate customer-facing notification and upcoming ETA for follow-up.

Example Slack snippet for status (#infra-releases)
------------------------------------------------
> Starting canary deployment for GPU runtime v2.0 (release_tag: 2026-02-10-v2). Canary nodes: gpu-canary-01/02. Monitoring: dashboard link. Oncall: @infra-sre-oncall.

Security and compliance checks
------------------------------
- Signed image verified with cosign and timestamp attestation.
- KMS keys rotated if release involves new encryption config.
- Audit logs for terraform and kubectl operations preserved for 90 days in org bucket: s3://redwood-infra-audit/releases/2026-02-10

Post-release validation and postmortem
-------------------------------------
- Validation: automated regression suite (quality and perf) run at T+6h and T+24h. Results uploaded to release PR.
- Postmortem: If any Sev is opened, publish a blameless postmortem within 72h with timelines, root cause, and action items.

Runbook annex: useful commands and snippets
-----------------------------------------
- Terraform plan: terraform -chdir=iac/gpu-pools plan -var=release_tag=<tag> -out=plan.out\- terraform apply plan.out\- kubectl rollout status deployment/gpu-runtime -n redwood --timeout=10m\- curl -sS https://status.redwood.ai/api/v0/incidents | jq .

Related pages and references
----------------------------
- Link to IaC module reference: confluence:eng-infra/terraform-and-iac/gpu-deployment-matrix-and-iac-promote-policy
- Link to GPU monitoring standards: confluence:eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/gpu-fleet-scaling-metrics-and-oncall-runbook

Appendix: precomputed capacity check example (CSV header)
-----------------------------------------------------
cluster,region,current_utilization,predicted_peak,headroom_percent
hosted-prod-west,us-west-2,72,85,15
dedicated-eu,eu-west-1,61,70,30

Notes and caveats
-----------------
- If the release touches networking (VPC/gateway changes), the Network Team must be looped in at T-24h and a separate rollback runbook must be opened.
- For on-prem/private deployments, coordinate with customer ops to schedule maintenance windows matching their timezone.

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary oncall: infra-sre-oncall (PagerDuty)
- Release lead contact: rina.patel@redwood.ai
- Escalation manager: marcus.huang@redwood.ai

----------------
